CMV retinitis (p.853) may be a cause of blindness, while chronic herpesvirus infections (p.853) may affect the skin and gastrointestinal tract. Recommendations have been published for both treatment2,3 and prophylaxis4 of opportunistic infections in AIDS patients. Recovery of immune function in patients responding to HAART may be sufficient to protect against certain opportunistic infections and to allow primary or secondary prophylaxis to be stopped.1,5 Other complications. Non-infectious complications of HIV infection include renal disease, metabolic and skeletal disorders, toxicities of HAART, and malignancies (be- low). Black patients with HIV infection may develop chronic or end-stage renal disease due to HIV-associated nephropa- thy (HIVAN) or thrombotic microangiopathy. Acute renal failure is common in hospitalised patients with (opportun- istic) infections, malignancies, or hepatitis C co-infection, while proteinuria is common in all HIV patients and may reflect an increased risk of cardiovascular events.
